questions.problem: A leaky pool is losing water. The amount of water lost after $t$ hours is given by the expression ${t}^{2}-t+3$ gallons, where $t\ge 0.$ What is the average rate of water loss over the first twelve hours?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(t)={t}^{2}-t+3$ be the amount of water lost in gallons after $t$ hours. To find the average rate of change of $f(t)$ from $t=0$ to $t=12,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[0,12]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δt} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(12)-f(0)}{12-0} \\  & =\frac{[(12)^{2}-(12)+3]-[(0)^{2}-(0)+3]}{12} \\  & =\frac{135-3}{12} \\  & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of water loss is $11$ gallons per hour.

questions.problem: Suppose that $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-t$ represents the position of a race car along a straight track, measured in feet from the starting line at $t$ seconds. What is the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t=1$ to $t=3?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $s(t)=2{t}^{3}-t$ be the position of the race car in feet after t seconds. To find the average rate of change of $s(t)$ from $t=1$ to $t=3,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[1,3]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δs}{Δt} & =\frac{s(b)-s(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{s(3)-s(1)}{3-1} \\  & =\frac{[2(3)^{3}-(3)]-[2(1)^{3}-(1)]}{2} \\  & =\frac{51-1}{2} \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of change of $s(t)$ is $25$ feet per second.

questions.worked_solution:
We have $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ if and only if $Δf=0.$ So

$$
\begin{aligned} & Δf=0 \\  & f(b)-f(a)=0 \\  & f(b)=f(a).\end{aligned}
$$

This means we have to find an interval  $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$

Since $f(2)=f(6)=3,$ we conclude that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=0$ on the interval $[2,6].$
